stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 5 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 10 observations with mean 46.1 % (within-hospital SD = 4.0). hospital B has 10 observations with mean 54.2 % (within-hospital SD = 5.8). hospital C has 15 observations with mean 73.7 % (within-hospital SD = 7.2). hospital D has 20 observations with mean 44.3 % (within-hospital SD = 3.7). hospital E has 20 observations with mean 40.6 % (within-hospital SD = 8.3). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 8.2 and 20.5 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital C: 73.3 % (shrunk from raw 73.7). Range [72.6, 73.5] as between-hospital SD varies from 8.2 to 20.5. Pooled mean: 50.8.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 50.8 % (weighted average of 5 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/15). At σ_between=13.7: B = 0.982.
Interval [72.6, 73.5] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (73.7) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (50.8) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
